validation/journeys/j13-schedule-notify.pg.test.ts::J13 M4-06 INT-003 INT-026 OPS-011 negative control: healthy destinations deliver every scheduled event once on the first attempt with no dead letter
oracle: On PostgreSQL the real scheduler fires a New York schedule over a cross-project list: the DST gap is skipped, an overlapping firing is forbidden, and the next firing publishes a new BatchRun with one Run per revision and cell, while a late tick records a misfire. While Slack answers 503, one webhook request times out after it was sent and a forged callback is refused by the egress policy, every event has exactly one delivery per destination, Slack and the forged callback end as visible dead letters, the webhook retries under the same delivery and event IDs, and no Run verdict, gate or Run count moves.

After the destination recovers, requeueing from the operations DLQ redelivers the first attempt's bytes under the same delivery IDs once each, the forged callback stays refused, and a second dispatcher or a restarted scheduler creates no further delivery. A control with healthy destinations delivers each event once on the first attempt with no dead letter. Only the Jira/Linear tracker part of J13 is M5.

oracle: Real SQLite connection refused before migrations on non-WAL storage and on NFS/SMB/FUSE statfs types; a second connection hitting the writer lock fails with UNAVAILABLE writer_contention within its busy timeout, never starts a transaction, and succeeds after the holder commits; after a SIGKILL around revision/admission commit no orphan revision/Run; exactly one of two OS processes wins a claim and a stale fence cannot finalize.

On PostgreSQL 17 through the synchronous bridge: a second OS process holding the writer transaction makes another writer wait and, after the 5 s lock timeout, fail with UNAVAILABLE writer_contention (reads stay available and never see uncommitted rows); a SIGKILLed writer releases the lock and leaves no rows; exactly one of two processes wins a claim; two concurrent migrators serialize on the advisory lock and apply each migration once; a scoped connection reads zero rows of another workspace in every table with a workspace_id, cross-workspace inserts are rejected, superuser and BYPASSRLS roles are refused, and the application, persistence, server and CLI suites pass unchanged on PostgreSQL.
items.note: Verified for the local SQLite profile: WAL with normal locking, foreign keys on, busy_timeout 5 s, a single controller writer, and refusal of non-WAL and NFS/SMB/FUSE storage before any migration. A busy writer lock surfaces as the typed retryable UNAVAILABLE error (reasonCode writer_contention) from BEGIN IMMEDIATE only; errors raised after the transaction started are not remapped. Migrations take BEGIN EXCLUSIVE directly and are outside this mapping. PostgreSQL has no runtime (ADR-002); its DDL mirror is not runtime support. M4 (F-A) adds the PostgreSQL runtime behind the synchronous PersistenceDatabase API (ADR-015): advisory-lock writer serialization, forced row-level security per workspace, byte-order collation, a migration lock, and a postgres-parity run of the application, persistence, server and CLI suites; the PostgreSQL profile still serializes writes on one host.

oracle: Revoked secrets, images and approvals cannot resurrect after restore; jobs and outbox are non-dispatchable and server tokens are invalidated; terminal identities are retained; the restore process opens no outbound connection and dispatches no outbox message; when the post-backup ledger cannot be read the restore declares postBackupLedger unavailable, stays suspended and review --apply refuses without --ledger-loss-accepted.
A restored GitHub installation that was revoked stays revoked after restoring a backup taken while it was active, and one that was never revoked keeps working.

A restored server starts isolated (operational_state restore:isolated and admission suspended_restore): admission is paused, schedules, integrations and outbox dispatch read application.operations.isolated() and do nothing, alert evaluation is skipped, and isolation ends only when an operator confirms the restore review and releases it; the DR rehearsal records the same gates on a fresh stack.

On PostgreSQL a real backup restored into a fresh database starts isolated with every integration paused and every token dropped: every registered server controller and the scheduler do nothing, no notification leaves, no check or comment is published and an inbound webhook is refused without being recorded, even after an administrator resumed the integrations. Only the owner may release, and only after the review; after the release the same pending schedule, notification and check proceed, the refused webhook delivery is processed on redelivery, and a schedule created by a revoked token stays paused as owner_revoked.
items.note: Verified for the local single-user profile. Restore replays secret, image, retention, deletion and approval revocations from the live ledger (it only tightens state, never reinstates). When the live ledger is unreadable or the live database has no workspace row, restore declares postBackupLedger=unavailable and exclusionsGuaranteed=false, writes restore_review=post_backup_ledger_unavailable, and review --apply requires --ledger-loss-accepted in addition to --revocations-confirmed. Review still opens admission only after the audited operator decision. A remote, lost-host ledger remains unavailable (M4). M4 S6: the scheduler controller does nothing while operational_state restore:isolated is set and resumes when it is released. M4 S8 notification dispatch sends nothing while the restore isolation flag is set. M4 S7 adds the revoked GitHub installation restore proof. S2b added the restore:isolated flag, application.operations.isolated() and the review-then-release gate. M4 proved scheduler, notification, GitHub and inbound-webhook isolation of a restored server-profile copy on PostgreSQL (restore-isolation.pg.test.ts).

oracle: Real SQLite databases at schema N-1 are upgraded through preflight, drain, backup, migrate and readiness. The backup is the old schema and is taken before migration. In-flight work stops the upgrade before backup or migration. A schema newer than the candidate, or a pinned revoked image, refuses the install or upgrade with a clear error and no mutation of the installation or database. A --keep-schema restore of the pre-upgrade backup is the only route to an older release. The same flow ran end to end between two real consecutive releases (see the smoke log).

A worker older than the database schema stops claiming and exits with worker_schema_behind while in-flight work finishes; a build that is ahead of or behind the database is refused until the migration or upgrade completes.
items.note: Verified for the local single-user profile only. Upgrade is offline: preflight, drain, backup, migrate, readiness. Rollback is allowed only when the installed schema is compatible; otherwise it is a planned restore with --keep-schema. Install, upgrade and rollback never write config, policy or secrets. Revoked image IDs are refused and are carried into restores. Not covered and not claimed: per-component rolling upgrades (the local profile has one controller with an embedded worker; resumption is a controller restart), distributed profiles (M4+), release signatures and license approval (other items). Approval revocations made after a backup are merged into the restored directory (OPS-025), and a restore that cannot read its post-backup ledger says so and stays suspended until --ledger-loss-accepted. The support matrix cites only repository paths that exist, and labels host facts that no repository file pins (Docker 29.x, host OS and kernel, image Node version) as observations. M4 added the per-component schema compatibility gate for workers and servers.

oracle: Untrusted TLS is refused before any login or request (browser login and request counters 0; runner server hits 0), while the same server succeeds through an explicitly pinned CA; an insecure-TLS network policy is refused at construction; cross-origin redirects drop authorization, cookies and API keys.

Server profile over real TLS (PostgreSQL, real HTTP server, TLS-terminating proxy): a client that does not trust the certificate fails the handshake before any request reaches the server; plaintext reaches only /health/live (a login password is refused over http); the session cookie is __Host-, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict and a cross-site write with it is refused for Origin and CSRF token; a correctly signed webhook over plaintext has no effect, a wrong, altered or unsigned one (even with a valid session cookie) has no effect, and a replay is answered from a durable record that survives retention purges.

Outbound webhooks: a plain http URL cannot be configured, a signing secret bound to another origin sends nothing, a consumer rejects a stale timestamp or wrong secret, loopback and redirect destinations are refused. GitHub sends no signed timestamp, so inbound replay protection is the delivery-ID record with the payload hash.
items.note: Local chain and hostname verification, insecure-TLS refusal, query-secret rejection and cross-origin credential stripping verified. The specification sentence that a private CA is preferred is a preference, not an acceptance criterion, and no user-facing CA option exists; it is not claimed. Server TLS, cookies, CSRF and signed webhooks are deferred to M4. M4 W2b proved the hosted surface over real TLS on the server profile (tls_required, __Host- Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict cookie, Origin and CSRF refusal, signed inbound webhook with dedupe/tamper and durable replay protection, https-only signed outbound webhooks with timestamp tolerance); the TLS-terminating proxy is a Node stand-in for Caddy and Caddy itself is proven by J17.

Secret rotate/revoke/release record the resolved reference id as the audit resource id, or the constant secret-reference when the secret cannot be resolved, never the name the caller used (secrets.test.ts: audits rotate, revoke and release by reference id and never by secret name). M4 added multi-organization export isolation (tenancy.pg.test.ts); retention windows remain with the operations slice. S2b enforced the declared metadata and audit retention windows per workspace.
